stem:
Facts:
1. Applicants for a business permit must submit Form A and Form B.
2. An application is complete only when all required forms are in.
3. Joel has submitted Form A but not Form B.

Which conclusion follows from the facts?
choices: Joel forgot to bring his copy of Form B.
Joel's permit application will be turned down.
Most applicants hand in only Form A at first.
Joel's application is not yet complete.
answer: Joel's application is not yet complete.
hints: Look at the rule for a complete application, then look at what Joel has done.
Joel is missing one of the required forms. What does fact 2 say about that?
Keep only the choice that must be true from the facts. Throw out choices that guess a reason, predict the future, or talk about other applicants.

solution.methodName: Facts-only test: keep only what the facts prove

steps.action: Fact 1: both Form A and Form B are required.
Fact 3: Joel has submitted Form A but not Form B.
Fact 2: an application is complete only when all required forms are in. Form B is missing, so Joel's application is not complete.
Check the others. The facts give no reason why Form B is missing. Joel may still hand it in, so being turned down is only possible. Nothing is said about other applicants.
The conclusion that follows: Joel's application is not yet complete.

This guesses a reason the facts never give. Joel may not have the form yet, or may still be filling it out.
trapNotes.Joel's permit application will be turned: This is merely possible. Joel may still hand in Form B and complete his application.
trapNotes.Most applicants hand in only Form A at f: The facts are only about Joel. They say nothing about what other applicants do.
